I swam to the edge, pulled myself up, and felt the sun on my wet skin. The voices in my head were quiet. For the first time, I knew that courage is not the absence of fear, but the decision that something else is more important. And I chose to live. The next time I stood on that board, I didn't hesitate. I simply jumped, because now I knew what waited on the other side—not safety, but a life fully tasted.

and each time I will find something new:
a shell, a stone, a curl of light on the water.

that some things are too big to be owned,
and that is exactly why they are beautiful.

Not the wings of a bird, but the wings of a dream I had carried since childhood.
I was standing on the edge of a cliff, not metaphorical but real,
and the wind was a dare.
Behind me, all the voices that said be careful, stay safe, don't jump.
Ahead, only the blue and the possibility of flight.
I closed my eyes and remembered every fall I had ever taken,
and how each one taught me to rise.
For the first time in my life, I did not calculate the risk.
I simply stepped into the air.
For one long, eternal second, I was falling.
Then I was flying.
The world opened beneath me like a flower,
and I laughed out loud, a sound I had never heard from myself.
It was the laugh of someone who has finally met their own courage.
For the first time in my life, I was not content to watch others soar.
I was the one in the sky.
Below, the earth looked like a map of all the places I had never been.
And I knew, with a certainty that burned, that I would go to every one of them.
